title: Earn Links to an MCP Directory
excerpt: Other sites link to a page that answers one question. A directory earns those links from READMEs, a handshake badge, dated counts, and corrections — not from bought posts.
coverImageAlt: Three pages a directory can earn a link to: methodology, a getting-started guide, and one server listing
newsletterSubject: Earn the link: point people at one URL that answers the question
newsletterIntro: READMEs, the handshake badge, and dated counts. The asks that get influzer.ai linked, and the ones to skip.
newsletterPullQuote: A link is a vote for one URL. The homepage rarely earns it.
contentHtml:
A link is a vote for one URL. The homepage of a directory rarely earns it. A page that answers one question does: what a handshake is, how to connect a first server, or where a specific server’s install snippet lives.

This is the link plan for Influzer.ai. It is also the plan for anyone publishing an MCP server who wants their listing, and the directory, cited in READMEs, docs, and AI answers. Search engines and answer engines use the same raw material. A page that is easy to quote is a page that is easy to link.

What a link is for

SEO still counts links from other sites. A link from a README or a docs page tells a crawler that this URL is the source for that topic. Generative engine optimization, GEO, asks a second question: can a model lift a sentence from that page and name the URL? The work is the same. Publish a page with a definition in the first paragraph, a date, and a limit. Then ask the people who already depend on it to point at that URL.

Bought links, link farms, and “write for us” blasts on unrelated blogs do not do this. They also do not survive a careful reader. Skip them.

Give each question one URL

Pick a small set of canonical pages. Update those pages when the facts change. Do not publish a second post that answers the same question with a different slug.

QuestionPage to link
What did you actually check?Handshake methodology. A handshake is initialize, then tools/list.
How do I connect one server?Get started with MCP servers
Where is the install snippet for this server?That server’s listing, /mcp/<slug>
What are the current counts?The homepage and the scoreboard. Cite the page. A number pasted into a post goes stale.
Is a green badge a safety approval?Not safe, just honest

Each of those pages should open with the answer. A model that has to skip a metaphor will cite the page that did not make it work for the sentence.

The link you can ask for: the author’s README

The person most likely to link Influzer is the author of a server that is already listed. They want install instructions in their README. The directory already has the snippet, the probe, and a badge.

On a remote listing, the README badge is an image from /api/v1/probe/badge?slug=your-slug. Indigo means live_ok, amber means auth_required, gray means unreachable. It is a handshake clock. It is not a SAFE badge. Stdio listings have no badge, because there is no public URL to call.

The badge image on the listing links to the probe for that endpoint. Add a normal text link to the listing as well. That is the URL you want crawled and cited:

[![MCP handshake](https://www.influzer.ai/api/v1/probe/badge?slug=your-slug)](https://www.influzer.ai/mcp/probe?url=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com%2Fmcp)

Install and tool list: https://www.influzer.ai/mcp/your-slug

Copy the badge markdown from the listing’s Embed tab so the probe URL matches the endpoint. The second line is the one that should sit next to the install command.

When a submission is approved, the email already includes the listing URL and invites a recipe. The follow-up that earns the link is shorter than a pitch: “Put this URL next to the install command.” Send it to authors who just shipped, not to a cold list of blogs.

Original facts beat another explainer

The web has enough posts titled “what is MCP.” It has fewer pages that will say, with a date, how many listed servers returned a tool list, how many asked for auth, and how many were unreachable. That is what the scoreboard is for. Link the scoreboard when you mention a count. If you quote a count in prose, include the date on the page you copied it from.

A handshake is not a safety review. Publishing that limit is part of why the methodology page is citable. A directory that implies “safe” will get the wrong links and the wrong citations.

A monthly note with three dated facts is enough: servers listed, servers with indexed tools, and the mix of live_ok, auth_required, and unreachable on the scoreboard. One page, updated. Ten thin roundups will not outrank it.

Corrections, registries, and one useful comment

Three places already talk about MCP servers. Show up there with one URL, after you have answered the question.

  • Corrections. When a post says there is no directory, mixes up WebMCP and an MCP server, or tells Claude to run a stdio command, reply with the page that draws the line. A website is not an MCP server and the first-hour guide are those pages. A correction that saves the author an edit gets linked. A drive-by “check out my site” does not.
  • Registries and lists. Awesome lists, the official MCP registry, and host docs sometimes keep a resources or directories section. One row, with the methodology URL, is the ask. A row that claims a SAFE badge will get removed.
  • The author’s own docs. Same markdown as the README. Docs sites pass more trust than a comment.

For a public comment, write the answer first. Link once, to the page that contains the detail you just gave. Submitting a server is the right link only when the person is trying to list one.

GEO is the same page, quoted

Answer engines cite pages they can fetch and compress. The GEO playbook covers crawlers, llms.txt, and definition-first pages. For this directory, the practical version is:

  1. Leave the methodology, the getting-started guide, listings, and the scoreboard crawlable.
  2. Keep llms.txt pointed at those URLs, not at every catalog row.
  3. Use one name, Influzer, and one domain, influzer.ai.
  4. Put the definition in the first paragraph. “A handshake is initialize, then tools/list” is a sentence a model can repeat.
  5. Once a week, ask a fixed set of questions in Perplexity, ChatGPT, and Google’s AI answers. “Where do I find MCP servers?” “What is an MCP handshake?” “How do I connect a server in Cursor?” Write down which URL was cited. Fix the page that lost before you write a new one.

A link and a citation fail for the same reason: the page did not answer the question the person, or the model, was holding.

A month of asks

  1. Week 1. Read the five URLs in the table above. Confirm each one answers its question in the first screen.
  2. Week 2. For the newest approved remote servers, send the badge markdown and the listing URL. Ask for both in the README, next to install.
  3. Week 3. Update the directory’s row on any resources list you already belong to. Pitch one list that has a directories section and does not have Influzer yet. Lead with the methodology, not a slogan.
  4. Week 4. Run the ten-question citation check. Change the weakest canonical page. Do not open a second URL for the same question.

Quick answers

Should the homepage be the link we request?

Only when the sentence is “this is the directory.” For a how-to, link the guide. For a count, link the scoreboard. For one server, link that listing.

Does the handshake badge count as a backlink?

The image is served by Influzer, and the markdown link points at Influzer. That helps. The text link to /mcp/<slug> is the one that tells a crawler which listing you mean. Use both.

Will guest posts on marketing blogs move this?

A post on a site that does not discuss MCP, agents, or developer tools rarely gets crawled as a source later. A README from a server people install is the better hour.

Can a sponsored slot buy rank or a citation?

No. A sponsored placement is a labeled ad. Rank is not for sale, and a handshake is not included.

Where to point the next link

  • Handshake methodology
  • Get started with MCP servers
  • Handshake scoreboard
  • Probe an HTTPS endpoint
  • What GEO is

Earn the link by being the page that answers the question. Then ask the person who already needed that answer to use the URL.
